abstract: The Capsicum genus encompasses remarkable genetic and phenotypic diversity underlying its agricultural, economic, and cultural importance. Here, we present a Capsicum super-pangenome constructed from 48 chromosome-scale genomes, including 38 newly assembled, spanning all five domesticated taxa and their wild relatives. We identified 72,687 pangene families and abundant structural variants (SVs), revealing lineage-specific gene-content dynamics and patterns consistent with strong purifying selection against large SVs. A pan-NLRome revealed extensive presence-absence variation in the disease-resistance gene repertoire, with domesticated accessions harboring fewer NLRs than their wild progenitors. The graph-based super-pangenome enabled extensive genome-wide association mapping and robust genomic prediction across 130 agronomic and metabolic traits, leading to the identification and functional validation of RAP2 as a regulator of carotenoid accumulation and the discovery of a structurally complex terpene synthase locus associated with sesquiterpene ylangene. Pangenome-wide dissection of capsaicinoid biosynthesis further revealed evolutionary remodeling of the pathway through tandem gene duplication, interchromosomal rearrangement, and regulatory specialization. Collectively, our findings illuminate the genomic basis of Capsicum domestication and metabolic diversity and establish a comprehensive resource for genomics-assisted improvement of disease resistance, fruit quality, and flavor.
